qa.q: A bisector splits ∠AOB into two angles of 35° each. What is ∠AOB?
qa.e: Both halves together: 35 + 35 = 70°.

qa.q: Ishita measured a triangle's angles as 60°, 60° and 80°. What can we say?
qa.a: There is a measuring mistake, because they add to 200°, not 180°
qa.e: The angles of a triangle add to 180°, so 200° means a mistake.

qa.q: Arm OA lies on the base line where the OUTER scale reads 0. Arm OB crosses 30 on the inner scale and 150 on the outer scale. What is ∠AOB?
qa.e: Read the scale whose 0 is on arm OA: the outer scale. It shows 150°.

qa.q: To draw ∠XYZ = 40°, where should the protractor's centre be?
qa.e: Y is the vertex (middle letter), so the centre goes on Y.

qa.q: Kriti wants to draw a 75° angle, but she marks her dot at 75 on the WRONG scale (the one that does not start at 0 on her arm). What angle does she actually draw?
qa.e: On the correct scale that point reads 180 − 75 = 105°, so she draws 105°.

qa.q: To draw a reflex angle of 300°, which angle can you draw first?
qa.e: 360 − 300 = 60°. Draw 60°, then the reflex angle is the outside part.

qa.q: In the estimation game Manav guesses 50° and the angle measures 62°. By how many degrees was he off?
Which angle is a good first guess for an angle that is just a bit wider than the corner of a page?
qa.e: A page corner is 90°, so a bit wider is about 95°.

qa.q: To copy ∠ABC onto another page, what should you do first?
qa.e: Measure the angle, then draw a new angle with the same measure.

qa.q: Ritu draws ∠PQR = 110°. Which type of angle is it?
qa.e: 110° is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse.

qa.q: To draw 135°, a quick way is to draw a straight angle and then…
qa.e: 180 − 45 = 135, so draw the straight angle and mark 45° back from one side.

qa.q: What type of angle is 72°?
qa.e: 72° is less than 90°, so it is acute.

qa.q: What type of angle is 145°?
qa.e: 145° is more than 90° and less than 180°, so it is obtuse.

qa.q: The hands of a clock at 3:00 make which type of angle?
qa.e: At 3:00 the hands are 3 × 30° = 90° apart, which is a right angle.

qa.q: Aisha opens a book flat on the table so its two covers lie in one straight line. What angle do the covers make?
qa.e: Covers lying in one straight line make a straight angle of 180°.

qa.q: Which of these is a reflex angle?
qa.e: A reflex angle is between 180° and 360°. Only 250° fits.

qa.q: Two lines cross so that all four angles are right angles. What are these lines called?
qa.e: Lines that meet at right angles are perpendicular. Parallel lines never meet at all.

qa.q: Joseph says the smaller angle between the clock hands at 10:00 is obtuse. Is he right?
qa.a: No, it is 60°, an acute angle
qa.e: From 10 to 12 is 2 hour-gaps: 2 × 30° = 60°, which is acute.

qa.q: An angle is split into two equal parts of 50° each. What type is the whole angle?
qa.e: The whole angle is 50° + 50° = 100°, which is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse.

qa.q: A ray on a straight line makes angles of 72° and x. What is x?
What is the angle between two neighbouring spokes of the Ashoka Chakra (24 spokes)?
In the Ashoka Chakra, what is the angle between one spoke and the spoke 6 places away?
qa.e: 6 gaps of 15° each = 90°.

qa.q: Two angles on a straight line are equal. What is each?
qa.e: 180 ÷ 2 = 90°, so each is a right angle.

qa.q: A see-saw plank makes an angle of 35° with the ground on one side. What angle does it make on the other side (along the ground line)?
qa.e: The two angles on the straight ground add to 180°: 180 − 35 = 145°.

qa.q: In the letter Y, the stem makes 150° with each arm. What is the angle between the two arms?
qa.e: The angles round the joint make 360°: 360 − 150 − 150 = 60°.

qa.q: Three angles sit side by side on a straight line: 40°, 75° and x. What is x?
Zoya draws the letter M with straight up-and-down outer strokes. What kind of angle is at each top corner?
qa.e: Each top corner of M is a sharp point, so the angle is less than 90°.

qa.q: In 'Platform number 4', the number is used to…
qa.e: The number names the platform; it does not count anything.

qa.q: Which sentence uses a number to measure?
qa.e: 6 m is a length, so it measures.

qa.q: Four children in a row say 0, 1, ?, 0. What must the third child say?
qa.e: Child 4 says 0, so child 4 is taller than child 3. Child 1 says 0, so child 1 is taller than child 2; child 2 says 1, so child 3 is shorter than child 2. Both neighbours of child 3 are taller: it says 2.

qa.q: In the taller-neighbour game, which child must say 0?
qa.e: No one is taller than the tallest child.

qa.q: Can a child at the end of the row say 2?
qa.a: No, an end child has only one neighbour
qa.e: An end child has one neighbour, so at most 1.

qa.q: Five children in a row say 1, 0, 2, 0, 1. Which children are taller than both their neighbours?
qa.e: Children saying 0 have no taller neighbour, so the 2nd and 4th are the 'peaks'.

qa.q: Three children say 1, 1, 1. Why is this impossible?
qa.a: If both ends say 1, the middle child is taller than both and must say 0
qa.e: Both end children have only the middle child as a neighbour, so the middle one is taller than both and says 0.

qa.q: A row of 4 children says 0, 1, 2, 0. Is this possible?
qa.e: Heights 4, 3, 1, 2 (in that order) work: the answers are 0, 1, 2, 0.

qa.q: In the row 12, 30, 25, 41, 18, how many supercells are there?
qa.e: 30 beats 12 and 25; 41 beats 25 and 18. 12, 25 and 18 each have a bigger neighbour. So 2.

qa.q: Why can the smallest number in a table never be a supercell?
qa.a: Because all its neighbours are bigger
qa.e: Every other number is bigger, so its neighbours are bigger.

qa.q: In the table 7 2 / 3 9, which numbers are supercells?
qa.e: 7: neighbours 2 and 3 → supercell. 9: neighbours 2 and 3 → supercell.

qa.q: What is the greatest number of supercells possible in a row of 7 cells?
qa.e: Supercells cannot sit side by side, so use cells 1, 3, 5, 7: 4 supercells.

qa.q: A 3 by 3 table holds 1 to 9. To get 5 supercells, where should 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 go?
qa.a: In the four corners and the centre
qa.e: Corners and the centre never touch each other, and each touches only edge cells holding 1 to 4.

qa.q: Fill the row 4, ?, 6 so that the middle cell is a supercell. Which number works?
qa.e: The middle number must beat both 4 and 6, so it must be more than 6: 7.

qa.q: In the table 5 8 1 / 2 6 9, how many supercells are there?
qa.e: 8: neighbours 5, 1, 6 → yes. 9: neighbours 1, 6 → yes. 5 (8 bigger), 1, 2, 6 (8 and 9 bigger) → no. So 2.

qa.q: Raju says: 'In my table no cell is a supercell.' Can he be right?
qa.a: No, the largest number is always a supercell
qa.e: With different numbers, the largest one beats all its neighbours, so there is always at least one supercell.

qa.q: Using 3, 8, 0, 6, 1 once each, what is the largest 5-digit number?
qa.e: Write the digits from largest to smallest: 8, 6, 3, 1, 0 → 86,310.

qa.q: Using 3, 8, 0, 6, 1 once each, what is the smallest 5-digit number?
qa.e: A number cannot start with 0, so start with 1, then 0, 3, 6, 8: 10,368.

qa.q: Using 5, 2, 9, 4, 7 once each, what is the smallest even number?
qa.e: An even number must end in 2 or 4. Ending in 4 gives 25,794; ending in 2 gives 45,792. The smaller is 25,794.

qa.q: Which number is written correctly with commas in the Indian system?
qa.e: In the Indian system the first comma comes after three digits from the right, then after every two digits: 3,45,678.

qa.q: On a number line, 0 and 1000 are 5 equal gaps apart. What number is at the 3rd mark after 0?
qa.e: Each gap is 1000 ÷ 5 = 200, so the 3rd mark is 600.

qa.q: A number line runs from 2000 to 3000 with 10 equal gaps. A dot is on the 7th mark after 2000. What is it?
qa.e: Each gap is 100, so the 7th mark is 2000 + 700 = 2700.

qa.q: Marks show 4,500, 4,800, 5,100 and 5,400 on a number line. Which is largest and what is the gap?
qa.e: The largest is the furthest right: 5,400. The gap is 4,800 − 4,500 = 300.

qa.q: Using 6, 1, 0, 8, 3 once each, which 5-digit number is closest to 60,000?
qa.e: 60,138 is only 138 above 60,000. The best below would start with 3 (38,610), which is far away.

qa.q: Is the sum 37 + 48 + 15 even or odd?
qa.e: Odd + even + odd: the two odd numbers make an even, and even + even is even. The total is 100.

qa.q: What is the digit sum of 9078?
How many supercells are in this row: 5, 8, 3, 6, 1, 4? (A supercell is bigger than all its neighbours.)
qa.e: 8 is bigger than 5 and 3; 6 is bigger than 3 and 1; 4 at the end has only one neighbour, 1, and is bigger. So there are 3.

qa.q: Start the Collatz game at 5 (even → halve, odd → × 3 + 1). What is the third number after 5?
qa.e: 5 → 16 → 8 → 4. The third number after 5 is 4.

qa.q: Arjun adds five odd numbers. The answer must be...
qa.e: Four odd numbers make two even pairs, and the fifth odd number makes the total odd. For example 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25.

qa.q: Which of these numbers has digits that add up to 10?
Meena says: 'Adding two even numbers always gives an even number.' Is she right?
qa.e: Each even number is made of pairs. Putting pairs together still gives only pairs, so the sum is even.

qa.q: Kabir looks at the numbers from 1 to 20. How many of them have a digit sum of 5?
qa.e: Only 5 and 14 (1 + 4 = 5) have a digit sum of 5 between 1 and 20.

qa.q: How many 3-digit numbers are there?
How many 5-digit numbers are there?
What is the smallest number whose digit sum is 23?
qa.e: With two digits the most is 18, so we need 3 digits. Make the end 9s: 5 + 9 + 9 = 23 → 599.

qa.q: What is the largest 3-digit number whose digit sum is 12?
qa.e: Put 9 first, then the rest (3) next: 9, 3, 0 → 930.

qa.q: The digit sum of 39 is 12. What is the digit sum of the next number, 40?
qa.e: 40 has digits 4 and 0, so its digit sum is 4. The 9 rolled over.

qa.q: Digit sums of 123, 234, 345, 456 are 6, 9, 12, 15. What is the digit sum of 567?
qa.e: Each one goes up by 3: 15 + 3 = 18. Check: 5 + 6 + 7 = 18.

qa.q: How many times is the digit 7 written when you write all the numbers from 1 to 100?
qa.e: Ones place: 7, 17, ..., 97 → 10 times. Tens place: 70 to 79 → 10 times (77 counts twice). Total 20.

qa.q: How many numbers from 1 to 50 have a digit sum of 7?
qa.e: 7, 16, 25, 34, 43: five numbers.

qa.q: Which of these numbers is a palindrome?
qa.e: 2442 backwards is 2442. The others change when reversed, for example 2424 becomes 4242.

qa.q: How many 2-digit palindromes are there?
qa.e: They are 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, 99, which makes 9. (00 is not a 2-digit number.)

qa.q: Do reverse-and-add on 48: 48 + 84 = 132. Then 132 + 231 = ?
qa.e: 132 + 231 = 363, which is a palindrome.

qa.q: Riya's digital clock shows 10:01. Is it a palindrome time?
qa.a: Yes, 1001 reads the same both ways
qa.e: Ignoring the colon, the digits 1-0-0-1 read the same forwards and backwards.

qa.q: What is the smallest 3-digit palindrome?
qa.e: The first digit must be 1 and the last digit must match it, so the smallest is 1_1 with 0 in the middle: 101.

qa.q: Which of these state languages is spelled as a palindrome in English capital letters?
qa.e: MALAYALAM backwards is M-A-L-A-Y-A-L-A-M, exactly the same.

qa.q: How many 3-digit palindromes start with the digit 5?
qa.e: They look like 5_5, and the middle digit can be any of 0 to 9: 505, 515, ..., 595. That is 10.

qa.q: Reverse-and-add on 23 gives a palindrome after how many steps?
qa.e: 23 + 32 = 55, which is already a palindrome. So it takes just 1 step.

qa.q: What is the sum of the smallest and largest 5-digit palindromes?
What is the difference between the largest and smallest 5-digit palindromes?
How many 3-digit palindromes can be made using only the digits 4 and 7 (repeats allowed)?
qa.e: First-and-last digit: 2 choices; middle: 2 choices. 2 × 2 = 4: 444, 474, 747, 777.

qa.q: How many 4-digit palindromes can be made with the digits 1, 2 and 3 (repeats allowed)?
qa.e: A 4-digit palindrome is a b b a: 3 choices for a and 3 for b. 3 × 3 = 9.

qa.q: I am a 3-digit palindrome. My digits add up to 13 and my middle digit is 5. Who am I?
qa.e: Outer digits are the same: a + 5 + a = 13, so a = 4: 454.

qa.q: I am a 5-digit palindrome. My first digit is 3, my second is double my first, and my middle digit is 0. How do you write me in words?
qa.e: a = 3, b = 6, c = 0 → 36,063: thirty-six thousand sixty-three.

qa.q: How many 5-digit palindromes start with 9?
qa.e: 9 b c b 9: 10 choices for b and 10 for c → 100.

qa.q: Which is the largest 5-digit palindrome that is even?
qa.e: An even palindrome ends in an even digit, so it also starts with that digit. The largest start is 8: 89,998.

qa.q: What is Kaprekar's constant for 4-digit numbers?
qa.e: Every 4-digit number (digits not all the same) reaches 6174, and 7641 − 1467 = 6174 again.

qa.q: Start with 2005. Arrange its digits largest-first and smallest-first, then subtract. What do you get?
qa.e: Largest: 5200. Smallest: 0025, which is 25. 5200 − 25 = 5175.

qa.q: Joseph uses 6174 in Kaprekar's routine. What does he get next?
qa.e: Largest 7641 − smallest 1467 = 6174. It comes back to itself, so the routine stops there.

qa.q: Why can't we use 3333 in Kaprekar's routine?
qa.a: All its digits are the same, so the answer is 0 at once
qa.e: 3333 − 3333 = 0, so the routine gets stuck. Other palindromes like 4224 work fine.

qa.q: For 3-digit numbers (digits not all the same), Kaprekar's routine ends at which number?
qa.e: For 3 digits the routine ends at 495, because 954 − 459 = 495.

qa.q: Aisha starts with 4321. What is the first subtraction answer?
Next step from 3087: the arrangements are 8730 and 0378. What is 8730 − 378?
Who discovered the special property of 6174?
qa.a: D. R. Kaprekar, a maths teacher from Maharashtra
qa.e: D. R. Kaprekar found this routine, which is why 6174 is called Kaprekar's constant.

qa.q: Run Kaprekar's routine on 2012. How many rounds to reach 6174?
Kaprekar's routine on 6264: 6642 − 2466 = 4176. What is the next answer?
Which date (DD/MM/YYYY) is a palindrome?
qa.e: 10/02/2001 → 10022001, which reads the same backwards.

qa.q: The date 20/12/2012 is special because…
qa.e: Written as 20122012, the block 2012 repeats.

qa.q: A clock shows 10:30. How many minutes until the next palindromic time?
qa.e: After 10:01 the next palindrome is 11:11. From 10:30 to 11:11 is 41 minutes.

qa.q: The clock shows 12:21. How many minutes until the next palindromic time (12-hour clock)?
qa.e: After 12:21 comes 1:01. 12:21 → 1:00 is 39 minutes, plus 1 = 40.

qa.q: A clock shows 5:47. How many minutes until the next palindromic time?
qa.e: Times after 5:00 look like 5:x5. 5:45 has passed, so the next is 5:55, which is 8 minutes away.

qa.q: Shreya was born in 2014. How many rounds of Kaprekar's routine turn 2014 into 6174?
Using only 3s and 5s and adding (repeats allowed), which number CANNOT be made?
Using 25s and 10s and adding, what is the fewest number of terms that make 70?
qa.e: 25 + 25 + 10 + 10 = 70 uses 4 terms. Three terms can make 60 or 75, but not 70.

qa.q: Which uses 9 and 4 (with + or −, repeats allowed) to make exactly 1?
qa.e: 9 − 4 − 4 = 1. The others give 9, 3 and 5.

qa.q: The sum of two 3-digit numbers is…
qa.e: The smallest sum is 100 + 100 = 200 and the largest is 999 + 999 = 1998. So it is a 3- or 4-digit number, never 2-digit.

qa.q: Two 4-digit numbers are added. Can the answer be a 5-digit number?
What is the largest possible sum of two 2-digit numbers?
qa.e: 99 + 99 = 198, so two 2-digit numbers can never add to 200 or more.

qa.q: A hall has 12 rows of 15 chairs, and 4 more chairs are added at the front. How many chairs in all?
Using digits 1 to 8 once each, Raghav makes two 4-digit numbers with the largest sum. What is the sum?
qa.e: 8642 + 7531 = 16,173: the biggest digits go in the biggest places.

qa.q: In the Collatz game, what comes after 9?
How many steps does 64 take to reach 1 in the Collatz game?
Why does every power of 2 reach 1 in the Collatz game?
qa.a: Because each halving gives another power of 2 until 1
qa.e: Halving 2, 4, 8, 16, ... always gives a smaller power of 2, ending at 1.

qa.q: Start the Collatz game at 12. How many steps until you reach 1?
What is the largest number reached in the Collatz chain starting at 7?
How many numbers from 100 to 199 have all their digits odd?
qa.e: Hundreds digit is 1 (odd). Tens: 5 choices, ones: 5 choices. 5 × 5 = 25.

qa.q: Which three of 16, 21, 35, 44, 50 add up to exactly 100?
Divya says the Collatz chain from 6 is 6, 3, 10, 5, 15, ... What is her mistake?
When is an estimate good enough?
qa.a: Guessing the number of people at a Diwali mela
qa.e: We don't need the exact number of people at a mela, but bills and medicine must be exact.

qa.q: Ishaan's heart beats about 80 times a minute. About how many times does it beat in an hour?
A school has 32 classes with about 30 students each. About how many students are there?
qa.e: 32 × 30 = 960, so there are about 960 students.

qa.q: Ritu walks about 2 steps for every metre. About how many steps does she take to walk 3 km?
In 30 seconds, estimate 498 + 301.
qa.e: 498 is about 500 and 301 is about 300: 500 + 300 = 800.

qa.q: A tap fills 1 bucket of 15 litres in 3 minutes. About how many litres does it give in an hour?
qa.e: In 60 minutes it fills 60 ÷ 3 = 20 buckets: 20 × 15 = 300 litres.

qa.q: Which is the best way to estimate how many words are on a 200-page book?
qa.a: Count the words on one page and multiply by 200
qa.e: Count a sample page, then multiply up to the whole book.

qa.q: Neha wants to make her own estimation question. Which one can she estimate sensibly?
qa.a: How many times does the school bell ring in a year?
qa.e: She can count rings in a day and multiply by the number of school days.

qa.q: In the game of 21 (add 1, 2 or 3), which number should you try to say just before 21?
qa.e: From 17, the other player reaches 18, 19 or 20, and you can then reach 21.

qa.q: In the game of 21, your friend makes the total 7. What should you add?
qa.e: The next key number is 9: 9 − 7 = 2.

qa.q: Why are the key numbers in the game of 21 four apart?
qa.a: Whatever the friend adds (1, 2 or 3), you can add enough to make 4
qa.e: If they add 1 you add 3; if 2 you add 2; if 3 you add 1. Each round adds exactly 4.

qa.q: In the game of 99 (add 1 to 10), the total is 80. What should you add to win?
qa.e: The next key number is 88: 88 − 80 = 8.

qa.q: What are the key numbers in the game of 99?
qa.e: Each round can be made to add up to 11 (1 + 10, 2 + 9, ...). So the key numbers are 11, 22, ..., 99.

qa.q: In the game of 99, who can always win if they play perfectly?
qa.e: The first player can't reach 11, so the second player lands on 11 and keeps landing on multiples of 11.

qa.q: In a new game players add 1 or 2, and whoever reaches 20 wins. What is the first key number below 20?
qa.e: Each round can add 3, so key numbers are 20, 17, 14, 11, ... 17 is just below 20.

qa.q: In the game of 21, the total is 18 on your turn. Can you win now?
qa.e: 18 + 3 = 21. You win straight away.

qa.q: What is computational thinking?
qa.a: Solving tasks with clear step-by-step procedures
qa.e: It means planning exact steps that can be followed, by a person or a computer.

qa.q: Which of these is still an unsolved problem?
qa.a: Whether every starting number reaches 1 in the Collatz game
qa.e: Nobody has proved the Collatz conjecture, though it works for every number tested.

qa.q: Which is a procedure?
qa.a: 'Arrange digits largest-first and smallest-first, subtract, repeat'
qa.e: It is a clear list of steps, like Kaprekar's routine.

qa.q: Why must a procedure for a computer be very exact?
qa.a: Computers follow each step exactly as written
qa.e: A computer cannot guess. Every step must be clear.

qa.q: In this chapter, numbers helped us do all of these EXCEPT…
qa.e: Numbers help with patterns, estimates and games, but they don't change the weather.

qa.q: A friend says the Collatz rule works for every number because it worked for 1 to 100. Is that a proof?
qa.a: No, checking many examples is not a proof for all numbers
qa.e: Examples suggest a pattern, but a proof must explain why it always works.

qa.q: How many steps are in this procedure: 'Pick a number. Double it. Add 6. Halve it. Subtract the number you picked.'?
qa.e: Pick, double, add 6, halve, subtract: 5 steps.

qa.q: Follow the procedure: pick 8, double it, add 6, halve it, subtract 8. What do you get?
A tally shows 3 bundles of five and 2 single strokes. What number is this?
qa.e: Each bundle is 5, so 3 bundles make 15, and 2 more strokes make 17.

qa.q: Meena asked her class how they come to school: Bus 12, Walk 8, Cycle 5, Car 3. How many children did she ask?
qa.e: Add all the frequencies: 12 + 8 + 5 + 3 = 28.

qa.q: Using Meena's data (Bus 12, Walk 8, Cycle 5, Car 3), how many more children come by bus than by cycle?
qa.e: 'How many more' means subtract: 12 − 5 = 7.

qa.q: How do you show 14 using tally marks?
qa.e: 14 = 5 + 5 + 4, so it is 2 bundles of five and 4 single strokes.

qa.q: Scores in 6 cricket matches: 45, 12, 67, 30, 89, 54. Arrange them from smallest to largest. Which score is third?
qa.e: In order: 12, 30, 45, 54, 67, 89. The third score is 45.

qa.q: At a Makar Sankranti fair, Kabir counts 20 kites: red 6, yellow 4, green 3 and the rest blue. How many kites are blue?
qa.e: Red, yellow and green make 6 + 4 + 3 = 13. The rest: 20 − 13 = 7 blue kites.

qa.q: What is the best way to find out the favourite sweet of the students in your class?
qa.a: Ask every student and record the answers with tally marks
qa.e: To answer a question about the class, collect data from everyone in the class and record it carefully.

qa.q: In a frequency table of favourite colours, what does 'frequency' mean?
qa.a: How many times each colour was chosen
qa.e: Frequency tells us how many times something appears in the data.

qa.q: Which question needs data to be collected?
qa.a: Which fruit do most students in our class like?
qa.e: Only the favourite fruit depends on what people say, so we must ask them.

qa.q: Ravi wants the favourite game of his class of 30. Whom should he ask?
qa.e: To know about the whole class, he should ask everyone in it.

qa.q: Which survey question is the clearest?
qa.a: 'Which do you like most: mango, banana, apple or guava?'
qa.e: A clear question with fixed choices is easy to answer and record.

qa.q: In a survey of 32 students, 14 chose cricket, 8 football, 6 kho-kho and the rest badminton. How many chose badminton?
From that survey (cricket 14, football 8, kho-kho 6, badminton 4), which conclusion is correct?
qa.a: Cricket was the most popular, chosen by 14 of 32
qa.e: Cricket has the highest frequency, 14 of 32.

qa.q: Tara surveyed 25 people about their favourite festival. Her tally total is 27. What should she do?
qa.a: Check her tallies, because she may have counted someone twice
qa.e: Frequencies should add to the number of people asked. 27 ≠ 25 means a mistake.

qa.q: In the cricket survey, how many more students chose cricket than kho-kho?
Why is it better to record survey answers with tally marks while asking?
qa.a: They make counting quick and in bundles of 5
qa.e: Tally bundles of 5 make it easy to count the total at the end.

qa.q: In a pictograph, 1 🍪 = 10 cookies. Riya's row shows 4 🍪. How many cookies did she bake?
qa.e: Each picture means 10 cookies, so 4 pictures mean 4 × 10 = 40.

qa.q: Key: 1 🚂 = 100 passengers. How many 🚂 pictures show 350 passengers?
qa.e: 300 passengers need 3 pictures and the extra 50 is half of 100, so half a picture: 3 and a half.

qa.q: A sweet shop sold laddoos in Diwali week: Mon 20, Tue 35, Wed 15, Thu 40. On which day were the most laddoos sold?
qa.e: 40 is the largest value, so Thursday has the longest bar.

qa.q: Using the same laddoo data (Mon 20, Tue 35, Wed 15, Thu 40), how many laddoos were sold on Monday and Wednesday together?
qa.e: Monday 20 + Wednesday 15 = 35 laddoos.

qa.q: Aisha's bar graph uses the scale 1 unit = 5 students. The bar for Kabaddi is 6 units long. How many students chose Kabaddi?
qa.e: Each unit stands for 5 students, so 6 units stand for 6 × 5 = 30 students.

qa.q: Four baskets hold 120, 80, 200 and 150 mangoes. Which scale is best for a bar graph in your notebook?
qa.e: With 1 unit = 20, the bars are 6, 4, 10 and 7.5 units long: they fit and are easy to draw. 1 mango per unit makes bars far too long; 1000 makes them tiny; 7 gives awkward numbers.

qa.q: Key: 1 🌳 = 8 trees. How many trees does half a 🌳 show?
qa.e: Half of 8 is 4.

qa.q: Joseph's bar graph shows that Class 6A read 32 books and Class 6B read 24 books. How many more books did 6A read?
qa.e: 32 − 24 = 8 more books.

qa.q: Key: 1 🥛 = 10 litres. Dairy A has 6 🥛, Dairy B has 4 🥛 and half a 🥛. How much more milk does A give?
qa.e: A = 60 L, B = 45 L, so 60 − 45 = 15 litres.

qa.q: Key: 1 🌳 = 20 trees. Village P has 5 🌳, Q has 2 🌳 and R has 3 🌳. How many trees in all?
qa.e: 10 pictures × 20 = 200 trees.

qa.q: Using that pictograph (P 5 🌳, Q 2 🌳, R 3 🌳), which village has the fewest trees and how many?
qa.e: Q has the fewest pictures: 2 × 20 = 40 trees.

qa.q: Rakesh says: 'Village P has more than double the trees of village Q.' (P = 100, Q = 40.) Is he right?
qa.e: Double 40 is 80, and 100 is more than 80.

qa.q: Key: 1 🎈 = 6 balloons. Asha sold 4 🎈 and Bina sold 2 🎈 and half a 🎈. Is Asha's sale more than double Bina's?
qa.e: Asha: 24. Bina: 15. Double 15 is 30, and 24 is less than 30.

qa.q: Key: 1 ⚽ = 8 goals. Team X has 3 ⚽ and a quarter ⚽. How many goals?
qa.e: 3 × 8 = 24 and a quarter of 8 is 2: 26 goals.

qa.q: A pictograph has no key. What can you say?
qa.a: Only which row has more pictures, not exact values
qa.e: Without a key you can compare rows but cannot find actual amounts.

qa.q: Key: 1 🍕 = 4 pizzas. Monday shows 9 🍕 and Tuesday 6 🍕. How many pizzas were sold in the two days?
qa.e: 15 pictures × 4 = 60 pizzas.

qa.q: Key: 1 🌻 = 5 flowers. How many 🌻 do you draw for 40 flowers?
qa.e: 40 ÷ 5 = 8 pictures.

qa.q: Key: 1 🚲 = 10 cycles. How should you draw 65 cycles?
qa.e: 65 ÷ 10 = 6.5, so 6 whole pictures and half a picture.

qa.q: Data: 12, 18, 30, 24. Which key makes every value a whole number of pictures?
qa.e: 12, 18, 30 and 24 are all multiples of 6.

qa.q: With the key 1 picture = 10, why is the value 37 hard to show?
qa.a: 37 ÷ 10 is 3.7, which needs 7 tenths of a picture
qa.e: Drawing 0.7 of a picture exactly is difficult, so pictographs work best with multiples of the key.

qa.q: Rina draws 9 🎫 for 45 tickets. What key did she use?
qa.e: 45 ÷ 9 = 5, so each picture is 5 tickets.

qa.q: Key: 1 🐟 = 20 fish. A fisherman caught 150 fish. How many pictures?
qa.e: 150 ÷ 20 = 7.5, so 7 whole pictures and half a picture.

qa.q: Which must every pictograph show?
qa.a: A title, the categories and the key
qa.e: Readers need the title, labels and key to understand it.

qa.q: Data: 200, 350, 500, 150 people. Which key keeps the pictograph short but easy to read?
qa.e: With 1 = 50: 4, 7, 10 and 3 pictures, all whole numbers.

qa.q: Using the vehicle data (7 am 200, 9 am 800, 12 pm 400, 6 pm 900), how many vehicles passed in all four hours?
How many more vehicles passed at 6 pm than at 12 pm?
A town's population (1 unit = 1000 people): 2000: 5 units, 2010: 7 units, 2020: 10 units. What is the trend?
qa.e: 5000 → 7000 → 10,000: the population keeps growing.

qa.q: In that town, by how many people did the population grow from 2000 to 2020?
qa.e: 10 − 5 = 5 units, and 5 × 1000 = 5000 people.

qa.q: Rainfall bars for June, July, August and September are much taller than other months. Why?
qa.e: Most of India gets its heavy rain in the monsoon.

qa.q: Ice-cream sales (in cones): Jan 50, Mar 150, May 300, Jul 200. Which month had the highest sales?
qa.e: May has the tallest bar: 300 cones.

qa.q: Using the ice-cream data, what is a sensible reason May sales are highest?
qa.a: May is the hottest month in many places
qa.e: Hot weather makes people buy more ice cream.

qa.q: Using the ice-cream data, May sales were how many times January sales?
Scale: 1 unit = 5 students. How tall is the bar for 45 students?
qa.e: 45 ÷ 5 = 9 units.

qa.q: Scale: 1 unit = 10 km. How tall is the bar for 75 km?
Which is NOT a rule for a good bar graph?
qa.a: Every bar must have a different colour
qa.e: Colours are optional; widths, gaps and the scale are what matter.

qa.q: A tally table shows Red 10, Blue 15 and Green 5. Using 1 unit = 5, what are the bar heights?
Where do the category names (like days of the week) go?
qa.a: Along the axis under or beside the bars
qa.e: Categories label one axis; values go on the other.

qa.q: The value axis is marked 0, 5, 10, 15, 25. What is wrong?
qa.a: 20 is missing, so the marks are not evenly spaced
qa.e: Marks must go up by the same step: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25.

qa.q: Scale: 1 unit = 20 trees. A bar is 6 units tall. How many trees does it show?
Kiran draws a bar 4 units tall for 60 mangoes. What scale did she use?
qa.e: 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so 1 unit = 15 mangoes.

qa.q: On a graph, the bar for 40 students is 8 units tall. What is the scale?
qa.e: 40 ÷ 8 = 5 students per unit.

qa.q: Same graph (1 unit = 5). One bar is erased but the table says 35. How tall should it be?
qa.e: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 units.

qa.q: A graph's scale is 1 unit = 10. The bar for 50 is drawn 4 units tall. What is the mistake?
qa.e: 50 ÷ 10 = 5 units, not 4.

qa.q: Children in families: 1 child: 6 families, 2 children: 8 families, 3 children: 2 families. How many children in all?
Marks in a 5-mark quiz: 3 marks: 4 students, 4 marks: 5 students, 5 marks: 1 student. What is the total of all marks?
How many students took that quiz (4 + 5 + 1)?
qa.e: 4 + 5 + 1 = 10 students.

qa.q: In a bar graph the gaps between bars are 1 cm, 1 cm and 3 cm. What should be fixed?
qa.e: Bar graphs need equal gaps between bars.

qa.q: A bar for 18 is 6 units tall. The bar for Sunday is 9 units tall. What does Sunday show?
qa.e: Scale: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 per unit. 9 × 3 = 27.

qa.q: Which data suits a vertical (column) graph best?
qa.e: Heights go upwards, so vertical bars match them.

qa.q: Which data suits horizontal bars best?
qa.a: Lengths of rivers like the Ganga and Godavari
qa.e: Lengths stretch across, so horizontal bars fit.

qa.q: An infographic shows one bag of rice for 100 kg and a bag twice as tall and twice as wide for 200 kg. What is the problem?
qa.a: The bigger bag looks 4 times bigger, though the value only doubled
qa.e: Area grows 2 × 2 = 4 times, which exaggerates the difference.

qa.q: What is an infographic?
qa.a: A graph decorated with pictures to share data attractively
qa.e: Infographics combine data with pictures and design.

qa.q: A graph shows scores 92 and 96, but its value axis starts at 90. The second bar looks 3 times as tall. Is that fair?
qa.a: No, the real difference is only 4 marks
qa.e: Starting at 90 makes 2 vs 6 units, which hides that the scores are close.

qa.q: Rivers: A 2500 km, B 1500 km, C 1000 km. With horizontal bars and 1 unit = 500 km, how long is bar A?
With 1 unit = 500 km, how many units longer is river A's bar than river C's?
qa.e: A: 5 units, C: 2 units. 5 − 2 = 3 units.

qa.q: What must every pictograph and bar graph state so it can be read correctly?
qa.e: Without the scale, we can't know what a bar or symbol stands for.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT a factor of 36?
qa.e: 36 ÷ 8 = 4 remainder 4, so 8 is not a factor. 36 = 9 × 4 and 36 = 12 × 3.

qa.q: How many factors does 20 have?
qa.e: Factor pairs of 20: 1 × 20, 2 × 10, 4 × 5. That gives 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, which is 6 factors.

qa.q: In the idli-vada game (idli for multiples of 3, vada for multiples of 5, idli-vada for both), which is the first number where Riya says 'idli-vada'?
qa.e: The first number in both the 3 and 5 times tables is 15.

qa.q: Which number is a common multiple of 6 and 8?
qa.e: 24 = 6 × 4 and 24 = 8 × 3. 36 is not in the 8 table, and 32 is not in the 6 table.

qa.q: Laddoos can be packed in boxes of 4 or boxes of 6. What is the smallest number of laddoos that fills boxes of 4 exactly AND boxes of 6 exactly?
qa.e: We need the smallest common multiple of 4 and 6, which is 12.

qa.q: What is the greatest common factor of 16 and 40?
qa.e: Factors of 16: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. The biggest one in both is 8.

qa.q: 6 = 1 + 2 + 3 makes 6 a 'perfect number'. Which of these is also a perfect number?
qa.e: The factors of 28 other than itself are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, and 1 + 2 + 4 + 7 + 14 = 28.

qa.q: Arjun says 1 is a factor of every number. Is he right?
qa.a: Yes, any number divided by 1 leaves no remainder
qa.e: Every number n = 1 × n, so 1 divides every number exactly.

qa.q: The treasure is at 36. How many different jump sizes take Jumpy exactly onto it?
qa.e: Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. That is 9 jump sizes.

qa.q: Which jump size will NOT land on a treasure at 40?
qa.e: 40 ÷ 6 leaves a remainder, so 6 is not a factor of 40.

qa.q: How many numbers from 1 to 90 are common multiples of 3 and 5?
qa.e: They are multiples of 15: 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90. That is 6.

qa.q: How many common multiples of 3 and 5 are there from 1 to 900?
What is the smallest number that can be divided exactly by every number from 1 to 10?
qa.e: 2520 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 × 7 has every needed factor. 1260 is not divisible by 8.

qa.q: Who am I? I am a factor of 30, I am odd, and I am bigger than 5 but less than 30.
qa.e: Odd factors of 30: 1, 3, 5, 15. Only 15 is between 5 and 30.

qa.q: Who am I? I am a multiple of 9 between 40 and 60, and I am even.
qa.e: Multiples of 9 between 40 and 60: 45, 54. The even one is 54.

qa.q: Ramesh waters plants every 4 days and Seema every 6 days. They both water today. After how many days will they next water on the same day?
qa.e: The first common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12.

qa.q: Which of these is a prime number?
qa.e: 37 has only the factors 1 and 37. 39 = 3 × 13, 49 = 7 × 7 and 27 = 3 × 9.

qa.q: How many prime numbers are there between 10 and 20?
qa.e: The primes are 11, 13, 17 and 19. That is 4.

qa.q: Why is 1 not a prime number?
qa.e: A prime must have exactly two factors. 1 has only one factor, itself.

qa.q: Write 36 as a product of primes.
qa.e: 36 = 2 × 18 = 2 × 2 × 9 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. Only the last form uses primes alone.

qa.q: Which pair of numbers is co-prime?
qa.e: 9 = 3 × 3 and 16 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 share no factor except 1. The others share 6, 5 and 7.

qa.q: Kabir says 91 is prime. Is he right?
qa.e: 7 × 13 = 91, so 91 has factors other than 1 and itself. (9 × 11 = 99, not 91.)

qa.q: What is the smallest composite number?
qa.e: 4 has factors 1, 2, 4 (more than two). 1 is neither, and 2 and 3 are prime.

qa.q: A number's prime factorisation is 2 × 3 × 7. What is the number?

Tara uses the Sieve of Eratosthenes for 1 to 100. She has crossed out the multiples of 2, 3 and 5 (but kept 2, 3 and 5). Now she crosses out multiples of 7, keeping 7. Which is the first NEW number she crosses out?
qa.e: 14, 21, 28, 35 and 42 were already crossed out as multiples of 2, 3 or 5. The first new one is 7 × 7 = 49.

qa.q: How many different rectangles can be made with 24 tiles (turning a rectangle doesn't count as new)?
Gita can arrange her beads in only ONE rectangle, a single row. How many beads could she have?
qa.e: Only a prime number of beads forms just one rectangle. 23 is prime.

qa.q: Which pair is a pair of twin primes?
qa.e: 17 and 19 are both prime and differ by 2. 21, 25 and 15 are composite.

qa.q: How many pairs of twin primes are less than 50?
What is the gap between the primes 89 and 97, and how many composite numbers lie between them?
What is the smallest number that starts a run of five composite numbers in a row?
qa.e: 24, 25, 26, 27, 28 are all composite, and 23 and 29 are prime. No earlier run of five exists.

qa.q: Using the digits 3 and 7 once each, which 2-digit numbers are prime?
qa.e: 37 and 73 are both prime.

qa.q: Which two primes add up to 20 and differ by 6?
qa.e: 7 + 13 = 20 and 13 − 7 = 6, both prime.

qa.q: Which pair is co-prime?
qa.e: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3, 35 = 5 × 7: no common prime, so only 1 is common.

qa.q: Are 9 and 16 prime numbers?
qa.a: Neither is prime, but they are co-prime
qa.e: 9 = 3 × 3 and 16 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 are composite, but their only common factor is 1.

qa.q: What is the first common multiple of the co-prime numbers 7 and 9?
qa.e: For co-prime numbers it is the product: 7 × 9 = 63.

qa.q: What is the first common multiple of 6 and 8?
qa.e: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24. 24 is also a multiple of 6. 6 and 8 share the factor 2, so it is less than 48.

qa.q: Treasures are hidden at 9 and 20. Which jump sizes bigger than 1 land on both?
qa.e: 9 = 3 × 3 and 20 = 2 × 2 × 5 share no factor but 1, so no jump bigger than 1 reaches both.

qa.q: Treasures are at 12 and 18. What is the biggest jump size that reaches both?
qa.e: Common factors of 12 and 18: 1, 2, 3, 6. The biggest is 6.

qa.q: A thread art circle has 12 pegs. Which gap makes the thread visit every peg?
qa.e: 5 and 12 are co-prime, so stepping by 5 visits all 12 pegs. Gaps 2, 3 and 4 share a factor with 12.

qa.q: With 10 pegs and a gap of 4, how many different pegs does the thread visit before it returns to the start?
qa.e: 0, 4, 8, 2, 6, then back to 0: 5 pegs. 10 and 4 share the factor 2.

qa.q: What is the prime factorisation of 84?
qa.e: 84 = 4 × 21 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7. All factors must be prime.

qa.q: Asha factorises 60 as 6 × 10 and Bilal as 4 × 15. What will both finally get?
qa.e: 6 × 10 = 2 × 3 × 2 × 5 and 4 × 15 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5. Same primes: every number has one prime factorisation.

qa.q: Which is the prime factorisation of 72?
A number has the prime factorisation 2 × 2 × 5 × 7. What is the number?
How many prime factors (counting repeats) does 96 have?
qa.e: 96 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3: six prime factors.

qa.q: What is the largest prime factor of 210?
qa.e: 210 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 7, so the largest prime factor is 7.

qa.q: Why is '4 × 3 × 5' not a prime factorisation of 60?
qa.e: 4 = 2 × 2 must be split further.

qa.q: Split 150 as 15 × 10. What is the full prime factorisation?
What is the smallest number with three different prime factors?
qa.e: Use the three smallest primes: 2 × 3 × 5 = 30.

qa.q: What is the smallest number with four different prime factors?
Using prime factors, which pair is co-prime?
qa.e: 35 = 5 × 7 and 39 = 3 × 13 share no prime.

qa.q: Does 24 divide 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5?
qa.e: 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 needs three 2s, but there are only two.

qa.q: 180 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5. Which number is NOT a factor of 180?
qa.e: 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 needs three 2s; 180 has only two.

qa.q: Is 14 a factor of 2 × 3 × 5 × 7?
qa.e: Both 2 and 7 appear, so 14 divides 210.

qa.q: Two numbers are 2 × 3 × 3 and 3 × 5 × 7. Why are they NOT co-prime?
qa.a: They both have 3 as a factor
qa.e: A shared prime factor (3) means they have a common factor other than 1.

qa.q: Rohit wants the smallest number that has 2, 3 and 7 as prime factors and is a multiple of 4. What is it?
Which number is divisible by 9?
qa.e: 4 + 5 + 3 + 6 = 18, which is divisible by 9. The others have digit sums 19, 13 and 11.

qa.q: Is 3416 divisible by 8?
qa.e: For 8, check the last three digits: 416 = 8 × 52, so 3416 is divisible by 8.

qa.q: Meena has 234 marbles. Can she share them equally among 6 friends?
qa.e: 234 is even and its digit sum 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 is divisible by 3, so it is divisible by 6. 234 ÷ 6 = 39.

qa.q: Which digit in the blank makes 52_ divisible by both 2 and 5?
qa.e: To be divisible by 2 and 5, a number must end in 0. So the number is 520.

qa.q: Which number is divisible by 4?
qa.e: The last two digits of 1732 are 32, and 32 = 4 × 8. 34, 26 and 50 are not multiples of 4.

qa.q: The number 7_2 is divisible by 3. Which digit could go in the blank?
qa.e: 7 + 3 + 2 = 12, which is divisible by 3. With 1, 2 or 4 the digit sums are 10, 11 and 13.

qa.q: Harpreet looks at 108000. Which fact shows quickly that it is divisible by 10?
qa.e: A number is divisible by 10 when its last digit is 0. Being even is not enough (for example 12).

qa.q: Is 2346 divisible by 6?
qa.a: Yes, because it is even and its digit sum 15 is a multiple of 3
qa.e: For 6, the number must pass the tests for 2 and 3. 2346 is even and 2 + 3 + 4 + 6 = 15 is a multiple of 3. (2346 ÷ 6 = 391.)

qa.q: Why do we check only the last two digits for divisibility by 4?
qa.e: Any number = (hundreds part) + (last two digits). The hundreds part is a multiple of 100, which is a multiple of 4.

qa.q: Why do we check only the last three digits for divisibility by 8?
qa.e: Thousands are multiples of 1000, which is a multiple of 8.

qa.q: What is the remainder when 7,859 is divided by 10?
qa.e: The remainder on dividing by 10 is the last digit: 9.

qa.q: What is the remainder when 7,859 is divided by 5?
qa.e: The last digit is 9, and 9 ÷ 5 leaves 4.

qa.q: Which year is a leap year?
qa.e: 2000 is a century year divisible by 400, so it is a leap year.

qa.q: Is 1900 a leap year?
qa.a: No, a century year must be divisible by 400
qa.e: 1900 ÷ 400 leaves a remainder, so 1900 was not a leap year.

qa.q: How many leap years are there from 2001 to 2040?
The remainder of a number on division by 2 is 1. What can you say about its last digit?
qa.e: An odd last digit leaves remainder 1 on dividing by 2.

qa.q: The sum of 5 odd numbers is…
qa.e: Odd numbers pair up into evens, leaving one odd left over, so the total is odd.

qa.q: Which is always true?
qa.e: Two odd numbers each have a 'spare 1'; together they make a pair, so the sum is even.

qa.q: Is the sum of two primes always even?
qa.e: Most primes are odd, but 2 is even, so 2 + 3 = 5 is odd.

qa.q: Which is the odd one out: 3, 5, 9, 7?
qa.e: 9 = 3 × 3 is composite; the others are prime.

qa.q: Which is the odd one out: 9, 16, 30, 49?
qa.e: 9, 16 and 49 are square numbers (3 × 3, 4 × 4, 7 × 7); 30 is not.

qa.q: A 2 × 2 grid of primes has row products 15 and 14, and column products 6 and 35. What is in the top-left box?
qa.e: Row 1: 15 = 3 × 5. Column 1: 6 = 2 × 3. The shared prime is 3.

qa.q: In that grid (rows 15, 14; columns 6, 35), what is in the bottom-right box?
qa.e: Top row: 3, 5. Column 2: 35 = 5 × 7, so bottom-right is 7. Check row 2: 2 × 7 = 14 ✓.

qa.q: Meena adds 13 + 27 + 35 + 41. Without adding, is the answer odd or even?
qa.e: Four odd numbers make two pairs, so the sum is even. (It is 116.)

qa.q: Riya's rangoli is a square of side 15 cm. She sticks ribbon all around its edge. How much ribbon does she need?
qa.e: A square has 4 equal sides, so the perimeter is 4 × 15 = 60 cm.

qa.q: The boundary rope of a school cricket ground goes around a rectangle 70 m long and 50 m wide. How long is the rope?
Arjun walks 3 times around a triangular park with sides 30 m, 40 m and 50 m. How far does he walk?
qa.e: One round is 30 + 40 + 50 = 120 m. Three rounds are 3 × 120 = 360 m.

qa.q: The perimeter of a square is 48 cm. How long is one side?
qa.e: A square has 4 equal sides, so one side = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm.

qa.q: A rectangle has perimeter 30 cm and length 10 cm. What is its breadth?
qa.e: Half the perimeter is length + breadth = 15 cm. So breadth = 15 − 10 = 5 cm.

qa.q: A regular hexagon tile has each side 8 cm. What is its perimeter?
qa.e: A hexagon has 6 equal sides: 6 × 8 = 48 cm.

qa.q: Which has the bigger perimeter: a square of side 6 cm or a rectangle 8 cm by 3 cm?
qa.e: Square: 4 × 6 = 24 cm. Rectangle: 2 × (8 + 3) = 22 cm. The square is bigger.

qa.q: Fencing costs ₹5 per metre. How much does it cost to fence a plot 20 m long and 10 m wide?
Sunil runs 7 rounds of a rectangular field 80 m by 40 m. How far does he run?
How many rounds of a 250 m track make 2 km?
A square garden has side 30 m. Asif starts at a corner and walks 200 m along the edge. How far is he along the side he ends on?
qa.e: One round is 120 m. 200 − 120 = 80 m = 2 sides (60 m) + 20 m.

qa.q: A wire is bent into a rectangle 15 cm by 9 cm. It is then bent into a square. What is the side of the square?
qa.e: Wire length = 2 × (15 + 9) = 48 cm. Square side = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm.

qa.q: A wire square of side 15 cm is reshaped into an equilateral triangle. What is each side?
qa.e: Wire = 4 × 15 = 60 cm. Triangle side = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 cm.

qa.q: Roshni lays a thread round a leaf and the thread measures 23 cm. What is the leaf's perimeter?
qa.e: The thread follows the boundary, so its length is the perimeter.

qa.q: Two friends run: Manu does 3 rounds of a 400 m track, Tanu does 5 rounds of a 250 m track. Who runs further and by how much?
qa.e: Manu: 3 × 400 = 1200 m. Tanu: 5 × 250 = 1250 m. Tanu runs 50 m more.

qa.q: Which is the best way to estimate the perimeter of a curved pond drawn on a map?
qa.a: Estimate, then check with a thread placed along the edge
qa.e: Estimate first, then a thread along the curve gives a good check.

qa.q: A 10 cm × 2 cm strip is cut into two 5 cm × 2 cm pieces and stacked to make a 5 cm × 4 cm rectangle. What is the new perimeter?
qa.e: New rectangle: 2 × (5 + 4) = 18 cm. (The strip had 24 cm.)

qa.q: In that rearrangement (10 × 2 strip → 5 × 4 rectangle), what happens to the area?
qa.e: The same paper is used, so the area stays 10 × 2 = 20 cm².

qa.q: A shape on a dot grid has 6 straight units and 2 diagonal units round its edge. Which is the correct way to write its perimeter?
qa.e: Diagonal and straight units are different lengths, so we keep them separate.

qa.q: Which is longer: 4 straight units or 4 diagonal units?
qa.e: Each diagonal unit is longer than a straight unit, so 4 diagonals are longer.

qa.q: A 12 cm × 1 cm strip is cut into three 4 cm × 1 cm pieces placed side by side along their long sides (forming 4 cm × 3 cm). What is the new perimeter?
qa.e: 2 × (4 + 3) = 14 cm, down from 26 cm.

qa.q: Two 3 cm × 3 cm squares are joined edge to edge. What is the perimeter of the new shape?
qa.e: It is a 6 cm × 3 cm rectangle: 2 × (6 + 3) = 18 cm. The joined edges are inside.

qa.q: In a pieces puzzle, Lata makes a square and then a long rectangle using all the same pieces. Which is true?
qa.e: The same pieces cover the same area. The long shape usually has a bigger perimeter.

qa.q: A square of side 4 cm is cut along a line into two 4 cm × 2 cm rectangles, which are put end to end to make an 8 cm × 2 cm strip. By how much does the perimeter change?
qa.e: Square: 16 cm. Strip: 2 × (8 + 2) = 20 cm. 20 − 16 = 4 cm more.

qa.q: Kabir's notebook cover is 20 cm long and 15 cm wide. What is its area?
qa.e: Area = length × breadth = 20 × 15 = 300 cm².

qa.q: A square carrom board has side 70 cm. What is its area?
qa.e: Area of a square = side × side = 70 × 70 = 4900 cm².

qa.q: A rectangle is made of 5 rows of unit squares with 7 squares in each row. What is its area?
qa.e: 5 rows of 7 squares = 5 × 7 = 35 unit squares.

qa.q: A room floor is 6 m by 4 m. Tiles of 1 m × 1 m cost ₹50 each. How much does it cost to tile the floor?
qa.e: The floor needs 6 × 4 = 24 tiles. 24 × ₹50 = ₹1200.

qa.q: A rectangle has area 48 cm² and breadth 6 cm. What is its length?
qa.e: Length × 6 = 48, so length = 48 ÷ 6 = 8 cm.

qa.q: Rectangle A is 6 cm × 4 cm. Rectangle B is 8 cm × 3 cm. Which is true?
qa.e: Both areas are 24 cm². The perimeters are 2 × 10 = 20 cm and 2 × 11 = 22 cm.

qa.q: Aisha cuts a 10 cm × 10 cm square of paper into 1 cm × 1 cm squares. How many small squares does she get?
qa.e: 10 rows of 10 small squares make 10 × 10 = 100.

qa.q: A square has perimeter 20 cm. What is its area?
qa.e: Side = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm, so area = 5 × 5 = 25 cm².

qa.q: Why are squares used as units of area?
qa.a: They cover a surface with no gaps or overlaps
qa.e: Squares tile completely and line up in rows and columns.

qa.q: Why are circles poor units for measuring area?
qa.a: They leave gaps when placed together
qa.e: Circles cannot cover a surface without gaps.

qa.q: A shape covers 9 full squares, 4 more-than-half squares and 6 less-than-half squares. What is its estimated area?
qa.e: 9 + 4 = 13. Less-than-half squares are ignored.

qa.q: A pond covers 15 full squares and 8 half squares. Estimate its area.
qa.e: 8 halves = 4 whole squares. 15 + 4 = 19.

qa.q: A map of a lake has 20 full squares, 6 more-than-half, 4 half and 7 less-than-half squares. What is the estimate?
Which part of a square should be ignored when estimating area?
qa.e: Pieces smaller than half are left out.

qa.q: Rekha traces her palm on 1 cm squared paper: 32 full, 10 more-than-half, 6 half and 9 less-than-half. Estimate her palm's area.
Each square on a map is 1 km × 1 km. A forest covers about 12 squares. What is its approximate area?
qa.e: 12 squares of 1 square km each is about 12 square km (12 km²). Area uses square units.

qa.q: A tangram square has area 64 cm². What is the area of one large triangle?
qa.e: Each large triangle is a quarter of the square: 64 ÷ 4 = 16 cm².

qa.q: In that 64 cm² tangram, what is the area of one small triangle?
qa.e: A small triangle is 1/16 of the square: 64 ÷ 16 = 4 cm².

qa.q: Which tangram piece has the same area as the medium triangle?
qa.e: The square, the parallelogram and the medium triangle each equal two small triangles.

qa.q: How many small tangram triangles make up the area of one large triangle?
qa.e: Large = 4 units, small = 1 unit, so 4 small triangles.

qa.q: Which rectangle of area 24 cm² has the largest perimeter?
qa.e: 1 × 24 gives 2 × 25 = 50 cm, the largest.

qa.q: What is the perimeter of a 3 cm × 8 cm rectangle?
Two rectangles both have area 18 cm²: 2 × 9 and 3 × 6. How much bigger is the first one's perimeter?
qa.e: 2 × 9: 22 cm. 3 × 6: 18 cm. Difference 4 cm.

qa.q: A farmer has 100 m² of land as a rectangle with whole-number sides. Which shape needs the least fencing?
qa.e: 10 × 10 has perimeter 40 m, the smallest of these.

qa.q: A rectangular sheet 8 cm × 6 cm is cut along a diagonal. What is the area of each triangle?
qa.e: The rectangle's area is 8 × 6 = 48 cm². Each triangle is half: 24 cm².

qa.q: An L-shaped room is made of a 5 m × 4 m part and a 3 m × 2 m part. What is its total area?
qa.e: 5 × 4 = 20 m² and 3 × 2 = 6 m². Together: 26 m².

qa.q: On a grid, a leaf covers 9 full squares and 6 half squares. What is its area?
qa.e: 6 half squares make 3 full squares. 9 + 3 = 12 square units.

qa.q: A square garden 10 m × 10 m has a square pond of side 2 m in it. What area is left for grass?
qa.e: Garden: 10 × 10 = 100 m². Pond: 2 × 2 = 4 m². Grass: 100 − 4 = 96 m².

qa.q: A tangram square has area 16 cm². Riya uses all its pieces, without overlapping, to make a cat. What is the cat's area?
qa.e: Rearranging the same pieces does not change the area, so the cat is 16 cm².

qa.q: A 2 cm × 2 cm square is cut out from the corner of a 12 cm × 5 cm rectangle. What is the area of what is left?
qa.e: 12 × 5 = 60 cm². The cut-out is 2 × 2 = 4 cm². 60 − 4 = 56 cm².

qa.q: Two triangles, each half of a 4 cm × 3 cm rectangle, are put together. What is their total area?
qa.e: Two halves make the whole rectangle: 4 × 3 = 12 cm².

qa.q: Joseph's T-shaped kite is made of a 6 cm × 2 cm top bar and a 2 cm × 5 cm stem. What is its area?
qa.e: Top bar: 6 × 2 = 12 cm². Stem: 2 × 5 = 10 cm². Total: 22 cm².

qa.q: A triangle sits inside a 12 cm × 8 cm rectangle on its 12 cm base, with its top corner on the opposite side. What is its area?
qa.e: Half of 12 × 8 = 48 cm².

qa.q: The top corner of that triangle slides along the top side. What happens to the area?
qa.e: The base (12 cm) and height (8 cm) don't change, so the area stays half the rectangle.

qa.q: A triangular flag has base 30 cm and height 20 cm. What is its area?
qa.e: Half of 30 × 20 = 300 cm².

qa.q: A house wall is an 8 m × 5 m rectangle with a triangular top of base 8 m and height 3 m. What is the total area?
A 10 cm × 6 cm rectangle has a triangle cut out of it, with base 10 cm and height 6 cm. What area is left?
qa.e: The triangle is half, so half (30 cm²) is left.

qa.q: Why is a triangle on the same base and height as a rectangle exactly half of it?
qa.a: A line down from its top corner splits the rectangle into two parts, and the triangle is half of each
qa.e: Each smaller rectangle is cut in half by a side of the triangle.

qa.q: A shape is made of a 4 cm × 4 cm square and a triangle of base 4 cm and height 4 cm on one side. What is its area?
A right-angled triangle has the two short sides 9 cm and 4 cm. What is its area?
qa.e: It is half of a 9 × 4 rectangle: 18 cm².

qa.q: With 18 unit squares, which arrangement has the smallest perimeter?
What is the perimeter of 10 unit squares placed in a single line?
qa.e: A 1 × 10 rectangle: 2 × (10 + 1) = 22 units.

qa.q: A figure has perimeter 16 units. A new square is added touching it along just 1 side. What is the new perimeter?
qa.e: The new square adds 3 edges and hides 1: +2. 16 + 2 = 18.

qa.q: A figure has perimeter 20 units. A square is placed in a notch where it touches 3 sides. What is the new perimeter?
qa.e: It adds 1 edge and hides 3: −2. 20 − 2 = 18.

qa.q: Two rectangles both have perimeter 24 cm: 6 cm × 6 cm and 10 cm × 2 cm. What are their areas?
Which has a larger area: a 7 × 3 rectangle or a 5 × 5 square? (Both have perimeter 20.)
Sana arranges 9 unit squares. What is the largest perimeter she can make (squares joined edge to edge)?
qa.e: A straight line 1 × 9: 2 × (9 + 1) = 20 units.

qa.q: What is the smallest perimeter for 9 unit squares joined edge to edge?
qa.e: A 3 × 3 square: 4 × 3 = 12 units.

qa.q: A house is 14 m long. The kitchen takes 5 m of that length and the hall takes the rest. How long is the hall?
That hall is 9 m long and 4 m wide. What is its area?
A plan shows a bedroom 4 m × 3 m and a study 3 m × 3 m. What is their total area?
Area maze: the left part has area 24 cm² and height 4 cm. The right part shares the height and has area 20 cm². How wide is the right part?
qa.e: Shared height 4 cm. Right width = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm.

qa.q: In that maze (left 24 cm², right 20 cm², height 4 cm), how wide is the whole rectangle?
qa.e: Left width 24 ÷ 4 = 6, right width 5. Total 6 + 5 = 11 cm.

qa.q: Which rectangle has area 16 cm² and perimeter 20 cm?
A rectangle is 10 cm × 6 cm. Which rectangle drawn inside it has exactly half its area?
qa.e: Half of 60 is 30, and 5 × 6 = 30.

qa.q: A square room has area 25 m². A rug 3 m × 4 m is laid on it. How much floor is left uncovered?
How do we read 3/8?
qa.e: The top number counts parts and the bottom names them: three-eighths.

qa.q: One paratha is shared equally by 4 children. What fraction does each get?
qa.e: Cut into 4 equal parts; each child gets 1 part: 1/4.

qa.q: 3 laddoos are shared equally among 6 children. How much does each get?
qa.e: 3 ÷ 6 = 1/2. Each laddoo is split in half.

qa.q: A shopkeeper weighs 'paav kilo' of tomatoes. How many grams is that?
qa.e: Paav means one-quarter: 1/4 of 1000 g = 250 g.

qa.q: 'Dedh' means 1 1/2. How many half-litre bottles fill 'dedh litre'?
qa.e: 1 1/2 litres = 3 halves.

qa.q: In Sanskrit, 'tripada' means which fraction?
qa.e: Tri = three, pada = quarter: three-quarters.

qa.q: Which is a unit fraction?
qa.e: A unit fraction has 1 on top: one part of equal parts.

qa.q: 5 friends share 1 big watermelon equally. Meena eats her share and Ravi's share. What fraction did she eat?
qa.e: Each share is 1/5, so two shares are 2/5.

qa.q: A pizza is cut into pieces of the same size. 6 of them make the whole pizza. What fraction is one piece?
qa.e: 6 equal pieces fill it, so each is 1/6.

qa.q: Riya cuts a square roti straight down the middle; Ravi cuts an identical one along a diagonal. Whose half is bigger?
qa.e: Both cut the same whole into 2 equal parts, so each piece is 1/2.

qa.q: A shaded triangle is one of 8 equal triangles that make a square. What fraction is shaded?
qa.e: 8 equal pieces fill the square, so each is 1/8.

qa.q: A strip is folded into thirds and then folded in half. What does each part show?
qa.e: 3 × 2 = 6 equal parts, each 1/6.

qa.q: How many 1/8 pieces fit into 1/2 of a strip?
qa.e: 1/2 = 4/8, so 4 pieces of 1/8.

qa.q: A rectangle is split into 3 equal strips; the middle strip is split into 2 equal halves. What fraction of the rectangle is one of those halves?
qa.e: Half of one third is 1/6.

qa.q: Which is the right way to check if a piece is 1/4 of a cake?
qa.a: See if 4 copies of it make the whole cake
qa.e: A piece is 1/4 if exactly 4 equal copies fill the whole.

qa.q: A paper is folded in half twice. 3 of the parts are coloured. What fraction is coloured?
qa.e: Two folds give 4 parts; 3 of 4 coloured: 3/4.

qa.q: In the fraction 5/12, what is the denominator?
qa.e: The denominator is the bottom number: 12, the number of equal parts.

qa.q: What does the numerator of 3/7 tell us?
qa.a: We take 3 of the 7 equal parts
qa.e: The numerator 3 counts how many parts we take.

qa.q: How many units of 1/9 make 7/9?
Which equals 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5?
qa.e: Four units of 1/5 make 4/5.

qa.q: To draw 3/8 of a strip, what should Aarav do?
qa.a: Cut it into 8 equal parts and shade 3
qa.e: Denominator 8: cut into 8 equal parts. Numerator 3: shade 3.

qa.q: A cake is cut into 10 equal slices and 7 are eaten. What fraction is left?
qa.e: 10 − 7 = 3 slices left of 10: 3/10.

qa.q: What is 9 × 1/11?
qa.e: 9 units of 1/11 make 9/11.

qa.q: Which fraction has numerator 4 and denominator 9?
qa.e: Numerator on top, denominator below: 4/9.

qa.q: The gap from 0 to 1 is split into 5 equal parts. Riya lands on the 3rd mark after 0. Which fraction is she on?
qa.e: Each part is 1/5, and 3 jumps of 1/5 make 3/5.

qa.q: Which is larger: 1/6 or 1/9?
qa.e: Cutting a whole into 6 parts gives bigger pieces than cutting it into 9 parts. So 1/6 > 1/9.

qa.q: Write 13/4 as a mixed number.
qa.e: 13 ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 1, so 13/4 = 3 wholes and 1/4.

qa.q: Arjun ran 2 3/5 km. Write this as an improper fraction.
qa.e: 2 wholes = 10 fifths. Add 3 fifths: 13/5.

qa.q: Between which two whole numbers does 17/5 lie?
qa.e: 17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2, so 17/5 = 3 2/5, which lies between 3 and 4.

qa.q: On a number line, each whole is split into quarters. How many jumps of 1/4 does it take to reach 1 1/2 from 0?
qa.e: 1 whole is 4 quarters and 1/2 is 2 quarters, so 1 1/2 = 6 quarters: 6 jumps.

qa.q: Kabir shares 3 rotis equally among 4 friends. What fraction of a roti does each friend get?
qa.e: 3 rotis shared by 4 means 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4 of a roti each.

qa.q: Which fraction is exactly equal to 1?
qa.e: 7/7 means all 7 of 7 equal parts, which is one whole. 7/1 is 7 wholes.

qa.q: Which fraction lies between 1/2 and 3/4?
qa.e: 1/2 = 4/8 and 3/4 = 6/8, so 5/8 is between them.

qa.q: Which fraction lies between 1/3 and 1/2?
How many fractions are there between 0 and 1?
qa.e: Between any two fractions there is another, so there is no end.

qa.q: On a number line from 0 to 1 split into 10 parts, where is 7/10?
qa.e: 7 jumps of 1/10 from 0 reach 7/10.

qa.q: Which point is exactly halfway between 0 and 1/2?
qa.e: Half of 1/2 is 1/4.

qa.q: Which fraction lies between 2/5 and 3/5?
Is 4/3 between 0 and 1?
qa.e: The numerator is bigger than the denominator, so 4/3 = 1 1/3 > 1.

qa.q: Halfway between 1/4 and 1/2 is…
Which fraction is equivalent to 3/4?
qa.e: Multiply the top and bottom of 3/4 by 3: 9/12.

qa.q: Write 24/36 in lowest terms.
qa.e: The greatest common factor of 24 and 36 is 12. 24 ÷ 12 = 2 and 36 ÷ 12 = 3.

qa.q: Meena ate 2/8 of a pizza. Harpreet ate 1/4 of the same-sized pizza. Who ate more?
qa.e: 2/8 in lowest terms is 1/4, so they ate the same amount.

qa.q: Which is bigger: 5/6 or 7/9?
qa.e: With denominator 18: 5/6 = 15/18 and 7/9 = 14/18. So 5/6 is bigger.

qa.q: Fill in the missing number: 4/7 = 20/?
qa.e: 4 × 5 = 20, so multiply the bottom by 5 too: 7 × 5 = 35.

qa.q: Aisha says 2/5 = 4/7 because she added 2 to the top and to the bottom. What is wrong?
qa.a: We must multiply or divide top and bottom by the same number, not add
qa.e: 2/5 = 4/10 (both × 2). Adding the same number changes the amount: 4/7 is bigger than 2/5.

qa.q: Which is the smallest: 1/2, 2/3, 3/8 or 5/12?
A chocolate bar has 12 equal pieces. Joseph eats 9 pieces. What fraction did he eat, in lowest terms?
qa.e: He ate 9/12. Divide top and bottom by 3: 3/4.

qa.q: On a fraction wall up to tenths, which fraction lines up exactly with 3/5?
Which piece on a fraction wall (halves to tenths) is the smallest?
qa.e: The more pieces the whole is cut into, the smaller each piece. 1/10 is smallest.

qa.q: On the wall, how many sixths line up with 2/3?
4 parathas are shared equally by 5 children. Which division fact describes one share?
qa.e: The wholes are divided by the number of sharers: 4 ÷ 5 = 4/5.

qa.q: Which addition fact shows 3 ÷ 7?
qa.e: 3 ÷ 7 = 3/7 = three units of 1/7.

qa.q: What is 5 × 1/8?
qa.e: 5 units of 1/8 make 5/8.

qa.q: Using the wall, which is larger: 3/8 or 2/5?
qa.e: 3/8 = 15/40, 2/5 = 16/40, so 2/5 is a little larger.

qa.q: On the fraction wall, which three fractions are all equal?
qa.e: They all line up with the half-way mark.

qa.q: Which is larger: 4/9 or 7/9?
qa.e: Same denominator, so the larger numerator wins: 7/9.

qa.q: Which is larger: 5/6 or 5/8?
qa.e: Same numerator: sixths are bigger pieces than eighths, so 5/6 is larger.

qa.q: Which is the smallest: 1/4, 1/9, 1/6, 1/2?
qa.e: All are unit fractions, and 1/9 has the most pieces, so it is smallest.

qa.q: Arrange 3/10, 7/10, 1/10, 9/10 in descending order. Which comes second?
qa.e: Descending: 9/10, 7/10, 3/10, 1/10. Second is 7/10.

qa.q: Ravi ate 2/5 of a pizza and Sita ate 2/7 of a same-sized pizza. Who ate more?
qa.e: Same numerator; fifths are larger than sevenths, so Ravi ate more.

qa.q: Which fraction is greater than 3/8 but has the same denominator?
qa.e: With the same denominator 8, a larger numerator (5) gives a larger fraction.

qa.q: Arrange 1/2, 1/3, 2/3 in ascending order. Which is in the middle?
Which pair is in the correct order, smaller first?
qa.e: Same denominator 11: 5 < 8, so 5/11 < 8/11.

qa.q: Riya drinks 2/9 of a bottle of lassi in the morning and 4/9 in the evening. How much does she drink in all?
qa.e: 2/9 + 4/9 = 6/9, which is 2/3 in lowest terms.

qa.q: A ribbon is 7/8 m long. Kabir cuts off 3/8 m. How much ribbon is left?

qa.e: 3/4 = 9/12 and 2/3 = 8/12, so the difference is 1/12.

qa.q: Arjun walks 1 1/2 km to school and then 2 1/4 km to the market. How far does he walk in total?
Mother made 1 whole cake. 2/5 was eaten at lunch and 1/3 at tea time. What fraction is left?
What is the right first step for 2/3 + 1/4?
qa.e: 12 is a common multiple of 3 and 4. Then 8/12 + 3/12 = 11/12.

qa.q: Meena says 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/8. What is the correct answer?
qa.e: Keep the denominator: 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2. (2/8 is only 1/4, which would mean the sum is no bigger than one part!)

qa.q: Uma painted 2/7 of a wall in the morning and 3/7 in the evening. How much did she paint in all?
qa.e: Same denominator: 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7.

qa.q: How much of Uma's wall is still unpainted?
A lace is 5/6 m long. Lata uses 1/3 m. How much lace is left?
On a number line in eighths, start at 1/8 and jump forward 5/8. Where do you land?
Kiran walked 1/2 km to the bus stop and 1/4 km from the bus to school. How far did she walk?
A movie lasts 3/4 hour. Raju has watched 1/3 hour. How much is left?
Which strip model shows 1/3 + 1/6?
qa.a: A 2/6 strip and a 1/6 strip end to end, making 3/6
qa.e: 1/3 = 2/6; with 1/6 more you get 3/6 = 1/2.

qa.q: Ammi has 7/8 litre of milk. She uses 1/2 litre for kheer. How much is left?
What did the ancient Indian word 'bhinna' refer to?
qa.e: Bhinna means broken, and it was used for fractions.

qa.q: How did the Bakhshali manuscript write fractions?
qa.a: Numerator above denominator, with no bar
qa.e: The numbers were placed one above the other; the bar came later.

qa.q: Who is credited with adding the fraction bar?
qa.e: The bar between numerator and denominator was introduced later by Al-Hassar.

qa.q: Ancient Egyptians mostly wrote amounts like 3/4 as…
qa.a: sums of different unit fractions such as 1/2 + 1/4
qa.e: They used unit fractions: 3/4 = 1/2 + 1/4.

qa.q: In which year did Brahmagupta write his rules for fractions?
qa.e: Brahmagupta wrote his work in 628 CE.

qa.q: Which unit fraction completes 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ? = 1?
qa.e: 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 = 7/8, so 1/8 more is needed to make 8/8 = 1.

qa.q: Which set of DIFFERENT unit fractions adds up to 1?
Which is a curve in the mathematical sense?
qa.e: A curve is anything drawn without lifting the pencil, including straight lines.

qa.q: Why use a compass instead of drawing a circle freehand?
qa.a: Every point is exactly the same distance from the centre
qa.e: The compass keeps a fixed opening, giving a true circle.

qa.q: Which letter can be drawn as one curve without lifting the pencil?
qa.e: O is a single closed curve. i, j and = need the pencil lifted.

qa.q: Which tool makes perfectly straight curves?
qa.e: A ruler guides the pencil along a straight path.

qa.q: A closed curve ends where it starts. Which is a closed curve?
qa.e: A circle comes back to its starting point.

qa.q: When is freehand drawing useful?
qa.a: For quick rough sketches and planning
qa.e: Rough sketches help us plan before an exact drawing.

qa.q: Is the number 8 a curve?
qa.a: Yes, it can be drawn in one stroke
qa.e: You can draw 8 without lifting your pencil.

qa.q: A compass opening of 3 cm is used. What is the diameter of the circle drawn?
qa.e: The opening is the radius; diameter = 2 × 3 = 6 cm.

qa.q: Riya opens her compass to 5 cm and draws a circle. What is its diameter?
qa.e: The compass opening is the radius. Diameter = 2 × radius = 2 × 5 = 10 cm.

qa.q: A bangle has a diameter of 6 cm. What compass opening draws a circle the same size?
qa.e: The compass opening is the radius, which is half the diameter: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.

qa.q: Which tool is best for drawing a circle?
qa.e: A compass keeps the pencil the same distance from the centre as it turns.

qa.q: Arjun draws an arc of radius 4 cm with centre A, and another arc of radius 4 cm with centre B. They meet at P. How far is P from A?
qa.e: P lies on the arc with centre A and radius 4 cm, so P is exactly 4 cm from A.

qa.q: Points X and Y are on a circle with centre O and radius 7 cm. What is OX + OY?
qa.e: OX and OY are both radii, so each is 7 cm. 7 + 7 = 14 cm.

qa.q: While drawing a circle with a compass, what must NOT change?
qa.a: The opening between the point and the pencil
qa.e: If the opening changes, the radius changes and the curve is no longer a circle.

qa.q: AB is 6 cm. Meena wants a point exactly 6 cm from both A and B. What compass opening should she use for both arcs?
qa.e: She wants the point 6 cm from A and 6 cm from B, so both arcs need a 6 cm opening. Joining the point to A and B makes a triangle with all sides 6 cm.

qa.q: Kabir opens his compass from P to Q, then puts the point on R and marks S with the same opening. What is true?
qa.e: The compass opening did not change, so RS is the same length as PQ.

qa.q: A wave of 3 equal half-circles fills a line of 18 cm. What is the radius of each?
qa.e: Diameter = 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cm, radius = 3 cm.

qa.q: For that wave (3 half-circles on 18 cm), where is the centre of the second half-circle, measured from the start?
qa.e: Second piece runs from 6 to 12 cm; its middle is 9 cm.

qa.q: A wave uses half-circles of radius 2 cm. How many fit on a 20 cm line?
qa.e: Each diameter is 4 cm; 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

qa.q: Which part of a circle is used to draw a smile?
qa.e: A smile is a curved piece of a circle: an arc.

qa.q: To draw a face with two eyes and a nose using a compass, which should you draw first?
qa.a: The big circle for the face
qa.e: Draw the outline first; then the other circles can be placed inside it.

qa.q: An eye shape is made by two arcs bulging in opposite directions. Where do the arcs meet?
qa.a: At the two corners of the eye
qa.e: The arcs join at the two pointed corners.

qa.q: Lata draws a wave of 6 half-circles each of radius 1.5 cm. How long is the wave's base line?
qa.e: Diameter = 3 cm; 6 × 3 = 18 cm.

qa.q: In a half-circle wave, the half-circles go alternately…
qa.e: Alternating up and down makes it look like a wave.

qa.q: Kabir draws a rectangle with one side 7 cm and the next side 4 cm. How long is the side opposite the 7 cm side?
qa.e: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so it is 7 cm.

qa.q: How big is each corner angle of a rectangle?
qa.e: All four angles of a rectangle are right angles, 90° each.

qa.q: One diagonal of a rectangle is 10 cm long. How long is the other diagonal?
qa.e: The two diagonals of a rectangle are always equal, so it is 10 cm.

qa.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at O. If AC = 12 cm, how long is AO?
qa.e: The diagonals cut each other into halves, so AO = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

qa.q: Aisha draws circles with the same centre and radii 2 cm, 3 cm and 4 cm. What are these circles called?
qa.e: Circles that share a centre are concentric circles.

qa.q: Which steps draw a square of side 5 cm?
qa.a: Draw a 5 cm line, make 90° angles at both ends, mark 5 cm up each, then join
qa.e: A square needs four 5 cm sides and four right angles. The last set of steps gives exactly that.

qa.q: Harpreet draws a circle of radius 3 cm. She draws a second circle of radius 3 cm whose centre lies on the first circle. How far apart are the two centres?
qa.e: The second centre is on the first circle, so it is one radius, 3 cm, from the first centre.

qa.q: Joseph wants to draw a rectangle with perimeter 20 cm and one side 6 cm. Which pair of side lengths should he use?
qa.e: Length + breadth = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm, so the other side is 10 − 6 = 4 cm.

qa.q: Which name correctly goes around the quadrilateral with corners P, Q, R, S in order?
qa.e: Corners must be listed in order around the shape: PQRS.

qa.q: In rectangle ABCD, which side is opposite AB?
qa.e: AB and CD do not share a corner; they are opposite.

qa.q: A square is turned so it stands on one corner. What are its angles?
qa.e: Turning a shape does not change its angles.

qa.q: In square WXYZ, which pair of sides are next to each other (adjacent)?
qa.e: XY and YZ share the corner Y.

qa.q: On dot paper, a tilted square has one side going 2 right and 1 up. What must the next side do?
qa.e: Turning a quarter turn: '2 right, 1 up' becomes '1 left, 2 up'.

qa.q: Which statement about a tilted rectangle is true?
qa.a: Its opposite sides are still equal
qa.e: Tilting keeps all lengths and angles.

qa.q: On dot paper, Kiran draws a shape with sides of steps '2 right 1 up', '1 left 2 up', '2 left 1 down', '1 right 2 down'. What has she drawn?
qa.e: All four sides use the same 2-and-1 step, turned by quarter turns: a tilted square.

qa.q: In quadrilateral ABCD, AC joins…
qa.e: A and C are not next to each other, so AC is a diagonal joining opposite corners.

qa.q: A rectangle is made of 2 identical squares placed side by side. Its width is 7 cm. What is its length?
qa.e: Length = 2 × 7 = 14 cm.

qa.q: A rectangle 24 cm long is made of 3 identical squares in a row. What is its perimeter?
qa.e: Side = 8 cm. Perimeter = 2 × (24 + 8) = 64 cm.

qa.q: Rectangle ABCD has AB = 10 cm and BC = 6 cm. P moves on AB and Q moves on DC. What is the shortest possible PQ?
qa.e: PQ is shortest when it is perpendicular, and then it equals BC = 6 cm.

qa.q: In that rectangle (10 cm × 6 cm), can PQ ever be shorter than 6 cm?
qa.e: Any slanted PQ is longer than the straight-across distance of 6 cm.

qa.q: A four-sided figure has angles 90°, 90°, 90° and 90°. One side is 9 cm and the next is 5 cm. What is the perimeter?
qa.e: Four right angles mean a rectangle: 2 × (9 + 5) = 28 cm.

qa.q: Why must a figure with four right angles have equal opposite sides?
qa.a: The two sides on the base are both perpendicular, so the top stays parallel and matches the base
qa.e: Perpendicular sides at both ends keep the top the same distance from the base.

qa.q: A rectangle 18 cm × 6 cm. How many 6 cm squares can it be broken into?
qa.e: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 squares.

qa.q: Can a 10 cm × 4 cm rectangle be broken into identical squares of side 4 cm with nothing left?
qa.a: No, 10 is not a multiple of 4
qa.e: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5, so a strip would be left over.

qa.q: What is the largest square that fits inside a 12 cm × 7 cm rectangle?
qa.e: The square's side cannot exceed the shorter side, 7 cm.

qa.q: After cutting that 7 cm square from the 12 cm × 7 cm rectangle, what is left?
qa.e: 12 − 7 = 5, so a 5 cm × 7 cm strip remains.

qa.q: Why should you draw a rough sketch before constructing?
qa.a: To plan the steps and see where lengths go
qa.e: Sketches help plan before the exact drawing.

qa.q: A circle of radius 2 cm is drawn with its centre 3 cm from the edge of a square. Does the circle stay inside (on that side)?
qa.e: The circle reaches 2 cm from its centre, which is 3 cm from the edge, so it stays inside.

qa.q: In a 10 cm square, the largest circle that fits has diameter…
qa.e: It touches all four sides, so diameter = 10 cm.

qa.q: For 'falling squares', each square is tilted 15° more than the one before. The first is not tilted. How much is the 4th tilted?
Shalini sketches a rectangle with a square inside it, touching three sides. The rectangle is 9 cm × 4 cm. What is the square's side?
qa.e: It touches the two long sides, so its side equals the width, 4 cm.

qa.q: Two 3 cm square holes are cut from a 10 cm × 10 cm square card. What area of card is left?
In rectangle PQRS, diagonal PR makes ∠QPR = 28°. What is ∠RPS?
qa.e: The two parts add to 90°: 90 − 28 = 62°.

qa.q: In square ABCD, what angle does diagonal AC make with side AB?
qa.e: A square's diagonal splits the 90° corner into 45° and 45°.

qa.q: In rectangle ABCD with ∠BAC = 50°, what is ∠ACD?
qa.e: ∠ACD = ∠BAC: the diagonal makes equal pairs of angles.

qa.q: A diagonal of a rectangle splits a corner angle into two parts. Which pair of parts is impossible?
qa.e: The two parts must add to 90°, so 60° and 40° (100°) is impossible.

qa.q: To construct a rectangle where the diagonal makes 30° with AB = 6 cm, what do you draw at B?
qa.e: BC must be perpendicular to AB; the 30° ray from A meets it at C.

qa.q: To draw a rectangle with AB = 4 cm and diagonal AC = 5 cm, what compass opening cuts the perpendicular at B?
qa.e: The arc is drawn from A with radius equal to the diagonal, 5 cm.

qa.q: In that rectangle (AB = 4 cm, AC = 5 cm), BC measures 3 cm. What is its perimeter?
Is a rectangle's diagonal always the bisector of the corner angle?
qa.a: Only when the rectangle is a square
qa.e: Only in a square are the two parts equal (45° each).

qa.q: A house outline (square + equilateral roof) has all sides 4 cm. What is the perimeter of the outline?
qa.e: The outline has 5 sides: 5 × 4 = 20 cm.

qa.q: In that house, what is the angle at the roof tip?
qa.e: The roof is an equilateral triangle, so each angle is 60°.

qa.q: Arcs of radius 5 cm are drawn from A and B. They meet at P. What is AP + BP?
qa.e: P is 5 cm from each: 5 + 5 = 10 cm.

qa.q: Which figure has 4 equal sides but is NOT a square?
qa.e: A rhombus has equal sides, but its angles need not be 90°.

qa.q: A rhombus has side 7 cm. What is its perimeter?
To make rhombus ABCD with AB = 5 cm, after placing D 5 cm from A, how do you find C?
qa.a: Arcs of 5 cm from B and from D meet at C
qa.e: C must be 5 cm from both B and D, so use equal arcs.

qa.q: A rhombus has one angle of 70°. Is it a square?
qa.a: No, a square needs all angles 90°
qa.e: With a 70° angle it cannot be a square.

qa.q: Why does the crossing point of two equal arcs from A and B lie at the same distance from both?
qa.a: Each arc keeps every point at the radius distance from its centre
qa.e: Each point on an arc is the radius away from its centre, so the crossing is the radius from both.

qa.q: What does symmetry mean?
qa.a: Parts of a figure repeat in a definite pattern
qa.e: Symmetry is about parts repeating in a pattern.

qa.q: Which has mirror (line) symmetry?
qa.e: A butterfly's left and right wings match.

qa.q: Which is a famous symmetric building in India?
qa.e: Its front is a mirror image across the middle.

qa.q: A flower with 6 identical petals looks the same after turning. What kind of symmetry is this?
qa.e: Its petals repeat as you turn it about the centre.

qa.q: Where is symmetry often seen in Indian art?
qa.e: Rangoli and kolam patterns repeat beautifully.

qa.q: A temple gopuram has carvings that are the same on the left and right of its centre. This shows…
qa.e: Left matches right across a vertical middle line.

qa.q: Which natural object usually shows symmetry?
qa.e: Most leaves are nearly the same on both sides of the middle vein.

qa.q: Which of these does NOT show symmetry?
qa.e: Crumpled paper has no repeating pattern.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
qa.e: A square has 2 lines through the middles of opposite sides and 2 along its diagonals: 4 in all.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
qa.e: Only the vertical and horizontal middle lines work. Folding along a diagonal does not make the halves match.

qa.q: Which capital letter has NO line of symmetry?
qa.e: R has a leg on one side only, so no fold makes its halves match. A and T have a vertical line; H has two lines.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular octagon have?
qa.e: A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as sides. An octagon has 8 sides, so 8 lines.

qa.q: Riya folds a paper and cuts half a heart shape along the fold. When she opens it, what is the fold line?
qa.e: Both halves of the heart were cut together, so they match exactly across the fold.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
qa.e: Each line goes from a corner to the middle of the opposite side. There are 3 corners, so 3 lines.

qa.q: Written in capital letters, which word looks exactly the same after folding along a horizontal line through its middle?
qa.e: B, O and X each have a horizontal line of symmetry. A, M, P and T do not.

qa.q: Arjun says a circle has exactly 4 lines of symmetry. Is he right?
qa.a: No, every line through the centre is a line of symmetry
qa.e: Any fold through the centre of a circle makes two matching halves, so it has unlimited lines of symmetry.

qa.q: A point is 5 squares to the left of a vertical line of symmetry. Where is its image?
qa.e: The image is the same distance on the other side.

qa.q: Why is the diagonal of a 6 cm × 3 cm rectangle not a line of symmetry?
qa.a: Folding along it, the two triangles don't sit exactly on each other
qa.e: Folding along the diagonal leaves corners sticking out.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a 6 cm × 3 cm rectangle have?
qa.e: Only the two lines through the midpoints of opposite sides.

qa.q: A point is ON the line of symmetry. Where is its image?
qa.e: Its distance from the line is 0, so it is its own image.

qa.q: The line of symmetry is horizontal. Point Q is 3 squares above it. Where is the image?
qa.a: 3 squares below it, in the same column
qa.e: Across a horizontal line, the image goes down the same distance.

qa.q: Shreya completes half a kite on squared paper. The top corner is on the line and the side corner is 3 squares left of it. How wide is the full kite?
qa.e: The side corner's image is 3 right, so the width is 3 + 3 = 6 squares.

qa.q: In a mirror, Vikram stands 2 m in front of the glass. How far is his image from him?
qa.e: The image is 2 m behind the mirror, so 2 + 2 = 4 m from him.

qa.q: Which line is a line of symmetry of a square?
qa.e: Folding a square along a diagonal makes the halves match.

qa.q: Paper is folded once and a hole punched through it. How many holes after opening?
qa.e: Two layers, so two holes, mirror images across the fold.

qa.q: Paper is folded in half 3 times and punched once. How many holes?
qa.e: Each fold doubles the layers: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.

qa.q: A half-circle is cut along the fold of a folded sheet. What shape is the hole?
qa.e: The fold gives the other half: a full circle.
