qa.q: Rina puts a blob of paint on one side of a fold and presses. What does she see when she opens it?
qa.a: A shape symmetric about the fold
qa.e: Pressing copies the blob as its mirror image.

qa.q: A paper is folded in half twice (into quarters) and a corner at the centre point is cut off. What is the hole like?
qa.a: A shape with 2 lines of symmetry in the middle
qa.e: The centre corner of all four layers is cut, giving one hole with both fold lines as lines of symmetry.

qa.q: A paper is folded once and then punched twice. How many holes appear when it is opened?
qa.e: Each punch makes 2 holes: 2 × 2 = 4.

qa.q: A row of paper dolls is cut from a strip folded zig-zag into 4 layers. How many dolls appear?
qa.e: Each layer gives one doll: 4 dolls.

qa.q: Which fold line is the line of symmetry of an ink-blot butterfly?
qa.e: The blot is printed as a mirror image across the fold.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with sides 7 cm, 7 cm, 7 cm have?
qa.e: It is equilateral, so it has 3 lines of symmetry.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with sides 6 cm, 6 cm, 4 cm have?
qa.e: It is isosceles: 1 line through the corner between the equal sides.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5 cm have?
qa.e: All sides differ (scalene), so no line of symmetry.

qa.q: Where is the line of symmetry of an isosceles triangle?
qa.a: From the corner between the equal sides to the middle of the opposite side
qa.e: Folding there makes the two equal sides lie on each other.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
qa.e: 3 through opposite corners and 3 through the middles of opposite sides.

qa.q: A triangle has exactly one line of symmetry. What can it be?
qa.e: Exactly one line means exactly two equal sides.

qa.q: Can a triangle have exactly 2 lines of symmetry?
qa.e: If it has two, it must have three equal sides and so 3 lines.

qa.q: A road sign is an equilateral triangle. How many ways can it be folded so the halves match?
qa.e: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry.

qa.q: What is the smallest angle of rotational symmetry of a square?
qa.e: A square looks the same after a quarter turn: 360° ÷ 4 = 90°.

qa.q: A ceiling fan has 3 identical, evenly spaced blades. What is the smallest turn that makes it look the same?
A rangoli looks the same after every turn of 45°. How many times does it match itself in one full turn?
qa.e: 360° ÷ 45° = 8 matches in a full turn.

qa.q: Which shape looks the same after a 180° turn but NOT after a 90° turn?
qa.a: A rectangle that is not a square
qa.e: A rectangle swaps its long and short sides after 90°, so it doesn't match, but after 180° it does.

qa.q: A regular hexagon is turned about its centre. What is the smallest angle that makes it look the same?
qa.e: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides: 360° ÷ 6 = 60°.

qa.q: Kabir's bicycle wheel has 12 identical, evenly spaced spokes. What is its smallest angle of symmetry?
Which of these has NO rotational symmetry (except a full turn)?
qa.e: F looks different after any turn less than 360°. S looks the same after a half turn (180°).

qa.q: Joseph says every shape with a line of symmetry also has rotational symmetry. Is he right?
qa.a: No: the letter A has a line of symmetry but no rotational symmetry
qa.e: Fold A down the middle and the halves match, but turn A and it looks different until a full turn.

qa.q: After its first step, the Koch snowflake looks like a six-pointed star. What is its smallest angle of rotational symmetry?
qa.e: The star has 6 identical points, so it matches itself every 360° ÷ 6 = 60°. Its order of rotational symmetry is 6.

qa.q: A wheel has 10 equally spaced spokes. What is its smallest angle of symmetry?
A figure's smallest angle of symmetry is 60°. Which of these is also an angle of symmetry?
qa.e: Angles of symmetry are multiples of 60°: 120°, 180°, 240°, 300°, 360°.

qa.q: Which can NOT be the smallest angle of symmetry of a figure?
qa.e: 360 ÷ 50 is not a whole number, so 50° can't be the smallest angle.

qa.q: A figure has arms pointing up, right and down only (equal lengths). What is its order of rotational symmetry?
qa.e: Turning 90° or 180° moves an arm to the empty left side. It matches only after 360°: order 1.

qa.q: Where is the centre of rotation of a ceiling fan?
qa.a: At the middle where the blades join
qa.e: The blades turn about the middle point.

qa.q: A rangoli has 8 equal petals. How many angles of symmetry does it have in a full turn (including 360°)?
qa.e: Smallest angle 45°, and 360 ÷ 45 = 8 angles.

qa.q: A figure has angles of symmetry 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°. What is the smallest?
qa.e: The smallest angle of symmetry is 90°, and the others are its multiples.

qa.q: A logo has 3 identical arms spaced 120° apart. What is its order of rotational symmetry?
How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
qa.e: Every diameter is a line of symmetry, and there are endlessly many diameters.

qa.q: Which turn makes a circle look the same?
qa.e: Every angle is an angle of symmetry of a circle.

qa.q: A circle has 8 equal sectors; sectors 1, 3, 5, 7 are coloured. What is the order of rotational symmetry?
qa.e: A 90° turn shifts by 2 sectors and keeps the pattern. 360 ÷ 90 = 4.

qa.q: A circle has 8 equal sectors; only sectors 1 and 5 are coloured. What is the order?
qa.e: Only a 180° (or 360°) turn keeps the pattern: order 2.

qa.q: A circle has 6 equal sectors. Which colouring gives order 3?
qa.e: Colouring every other sector matches every 120°: 360 ÷ 120 = 3.

qa.q: A circle has 12 equal sectors with sectors 1, 5 and 9 coloured. What is the smallest angle of symmetry?
qa.e: The coloured sectors are 4 apart: 4 × 30° = 120°.

qa.q: A 2 × 2 tile design has two plain tiles on the left and two tiles with vertical stripes on the right. How many lines of symmetry?

qa.e: F has no fold line and doesn't match after any part turn.

qa.e: From −3 up to 0 is 3 floors, and from 0 to 10 is 10 floors: 13 in all.

qa.e: 2 steps left reach 0, and 3 more steps reach −3.
